name: control-mapping-v1
description: Labelled control descriptions with the framework controls a governance reviewer would expect map_control to return. Labels are gold sets: a case counts as a hit at rank k if ANY of the listed controls appears in the top k for that framework. A null expectation means the framework is not evaluated for that case, which is itself a documented statement about coverage.
labelling_notes: Labels were written from the framework documents before running the tool, not read back from its output.
Where a framework genuinely has no close analogue for a practice, the expectation is null rather than a forced match. Forcing a label there would make the score look better and the tool worse.
Multiple acceptable controls per framework reflects real crosswalk practice: more than one clause legitimately covers most practices.

cases.description: A named reviewer must approve every AI-drafted customer communication before it is sent, and the reviewer can reject or edit the draft.
Every model inference is written to an immutable audit log with a seven year retention period.
We test the model for bias across protected groups before each release and document the fairness metrics we used.
We maintain a central inventory of every AI system in use, including shadow AI discovered on employee laptops.
Before onboarding a foundation model provider we run vendor due diligence covering security, data use and their model change practices.
All staff who operate AI tools complete annual AI literacy training appropriate to their role.
We run red team exercises and adversarial testing against the model before launch to find unsafe outputs.
A documented incident response runbook covers AI malfunctions, and we communicate incidents to affected users.
The chatbot tells users up front that they are interacting with an AI assistant and not a person.
The board receives a quarterly report on AI risk and the chief executive signs off on high risk deployments.
We record the provenance and lineage of every training dataset we acquire, back to its original source.
There is a documented procedure for decommissioning and retiring an AI system safely, including disposal of the model and its data.
Deployed models are monitored in production for drift and degradation against defined alert thresholds.
Organisational risk tolerance for AI is documented, and the level of risk management effort is set against it.
Before deployment we complete an impact assessment covering effects on individuals, groups and fundamental rights.
Technical documentation describing the system design, its knowledge limits and how outputs should be used is produced before release.
Training data is encrypted at rest and access is granted on least privilege with authentication enforced.
Personal data used by the model has a documented lawful basis and privacy risk has been examined.
End users can report a problem with an automated decision and appeal the outcome through a published channel.
An approved written AI policy defines acceptable and prohibited uses and is reviewed annually.
An independent internal audit assesses the AI management system at planned intervals and raises corrective actions.
There is a tested mechanism to deactivate or disengage a model that is behaving inconsistently with its intended use.
Images and audio produced by the generative system are watermarked and labelled as AI generated content.
The energy consumption and carbon footprint of model training is assessed and documented.
A written statement defines the intended purpose of the system and the uses that are explicitly out of scope.
An automated evaluation suite runs in the release pipeline with documented acceptance criteria and blocks a release on regression.
Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority within the required deadline.
Pre-trained models supplied by a third party are monitored for vendor updates as part of routine maintenance.
As a general purpose AI model provider we publish a summary of training content and maintain a copyright policy.
Changes are promoted to production through defined release gates with change control and version control applied.
